data.narrative:
Last Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Bret Kugelmass, has raised $140M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Antares operating in the nuclear energy sector.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using total capital raised ($140M) as a proxy for post-money valuation at Series B, application of a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C → Series D advancement yields $238M. A peer-median approach is not applicable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy subsector; while 4 same-sector peers exist, none meet the threshold of 3+ datapoints in narrow filters required for reliable cross-sectional pricing.

The triangulated valuation range is $202M (low) to $274M (high), with a median of $238M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty around appropriate step-up multiples for nuclear energy companies specifically and the representativeness of stage-progression benchmarks in a capital-intensive, pre-revenue or early-revenue subsector. Sector-specific dynamics—regulatory timelines, capital efficiency, and technology differentiation—should inform any final valuation decision beyond this quantitative framework.
